    "content": "import { faker } from \"@faker-js/faker\";\n\nexport const TRANSACTION_COUNT = 50;\nexport const RESOLUTION_DELAY_MS = 1500;\nexport const STARTING_BALANCE = 100000;\n\nexport type SettlementStatus = \"pending\" | \"cleared\" | \"failed\";\nexport type FundsOperation = \"credit\" | \"debit\";\n\nexport type Transaction = {\n  id: string;\n  clientName: string;\n  amountUsd: number;\n  status: SettlementStatus;\n  finalStatus: Exclude&lt;SettlementStatus, \"pending\"&gt;;\n  operation: FundsOperation;\n  timestamp: string;\n};\n\nexport type ResolutionResult = {\n  transactions: Transaction[];\n  balance: number;\n};\n\ntype ScriptTransaction = {\n  id: string;\n  clientName: string;\n  amountUsd: number;\n  status: SettlementStatus;\n  timestamp: string;\n};\n\nexport function normalizeScriptTransactions(\n  incomingTransactions: ScriptTransaction[],\n): Transaction[] {\n  return incomingTransactions.map((transaction) =&gt; ({\n    ...transaction,\n    status: \"pending\",\n    finalStatus: faker.helpers.arrayElement([\"cleared\", \"failed\"]),\n    operation: faker.helpers.arrayElement([\"credit\", \"debit\"]),\n  }));\n}\n\nexport function createFallbackTransactions(count = TRANSACTION_COUNT): Transaction[] {\n  return normalizeScriptTransactions(\n    Array.from({ length: count }, () =&gt; ({\n      id: faker.string.uuid(),\n      clientName: faker.person.fullName(),\n      amountUsd: Number(faker.finance.amount({ min: 10, max: 5000, dec: 2 })),\n      status: \"pending\" as const,\n      timestamp: faker.date.recent({ days: 30 }).toISOString(),\n    })),\n  );\n}\n\nexport function applyFundsOperation(\n  balance: number,\n  transaction: Pick&lt;Transaction, \"operation\" | \"amountUsd\" | \"finalStatus\"&gt;,\n): number {\n  if (transaction.finalStatus !== \"cleared\") {\n    return balance;\n  }\n\n  return transaction.operation === \"credit\"\n    ? balance + transaction.amountUsd\n    : balance - transaction.amountUsd;\n}\n\nexport function resolvePendingTransactions(\n  transactions: Transaction[],\n  openingBalance: number,\n): ResolutionResult {\n  let nextBalance = openingBalance;\n\n  const resolvedTransactions = transactions.map((transaction) =&gt; {\n    if (transaction.status !== \"pending\") {\n      return transaction;\n    }\n\n    nextBalance = applyFundsOperation(nextBalance, transaction);\n\n    return {\n      ...transaction,\n      status: transaction.finalStatus,\n    };\n  });\n\n  return {\n    transactions: resolvedTransactions,\n    balance: Number(nextBalance.toFixed(2)),\n  };\n}\n\nexport function countByStatus(transactions: Transaction[]) {\n  return transactions.reduce(\n    (accumulator, transaction) =&gt; {\n      accumulator[transaction.status] += 1;\n      return accumulator;\n    },\n    { pending: 0, cleared: 0, failed: 0 },\n  );\n}\n",
    "languageId": "typescript"
  }
}

settlementsScript.generateMixedAmountSettlementTransactions(\n            TRANSACTION_COUNT,\n          )\n        : [];\n\n    setTransactions(\n      generatedFromScript.length\n        ? normalizeScriptTransactions(generatedFromScript)\n        : createFallbackTransactions(TRANSACTION_COUNT),\n    );\n  }, []);\n\n  useEffect(() =&gt; {\n    if (!transactions.some((transaction) =&gt; transaction.status === \"pending\")) {\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const timer = window.setTimeout(() =&gt; {\n      setTransactions((currentTransactions) =&gt; {\n        const resolution = resolvePendingTransactions(currentTransactions, balance);\n        setBalance(resolution.balance);\n        return resolution.transactions;\n      });\n    }, RESOLUTION_DELAY_MS);\n\n    return () =&gt; window.clearTimeout(timer);\n  }, [balance, transactions]);\n\n  const value = useMemo(() =&gt; {\n    const statusCounts = countByStatus(transactions);\n\n    return {\n      transactions,\n      balance,\n      pendingCount: statusCounts.pending,\n      isProcessing: statusCounts.pending &gt; 0,\n    };\n  }, [balance, transactions]);\n\n  return (\n    &lt;TransactionsContext.Provider value={value}&gt;\n      {children}\n    &lt;/TransactionsContext.Provider&gt;\n  );\n}\n\nexport function useTransactions() {\n  const contextValue = useContext(TransactionsContext);\n\n  if (!contextValue) {\n    throw new Error(\"useTransactions must be used within a TransactionsProvider\");\n  }\n\n  return contextValue;\n}\n",

---

Built end-to-end in `portala` with context state, 50 incoming transactions, 1.5s pending resolution, funds operations, and tests (including use of `scripts/generate-settlements.js`).

### What I changed

- Added transaction domain/state logic in `portala/lib/transactions.ts`
  - `TRANSACTION_COUNT = 50`, `RESOLUTION_DELAY_MS = 1500`, `STARTING_BALANCE`
  - Types for status/operation/transaction
  - `normalizeScriptTransactions(...)` for script-generated input
  - `resolvePendingTransactions(...)` with clear funds operations:
    - `cleared + credit` => add amount
    - `cleared + debit` => subtract amount
    - `failed` => no balance change

- Added React Context container in `portala/context/transactions-context.tsx`
  - `TransactionsProvider` and `useTransactions`
  - Initializes 50 pending Faker transactions
  - Automatically resolves all pending transactions after 1.5s
  - Exposes global state: `transactions`, `balance`, `pending

Those logs show two separate issues:

- You first ran `npm` from the repo root (`/Portola`), which has no `package.json`.
- In `portala`, Vitest is picking up `tests/settlement-generator.spec.js` (a Playwright test), and `framer-motion` wasn’t installed when that run started.

I fixed the Vitest side by scoping it to `*.test.ts/tsx` only in `portala/vitest.config.ts`, so it won’t run Playwright specs.

Run from here:

```bash
cd ~/projects/Portola/portala
npm install
npm run test:watch
```

If `framer-motion` still errors, install explicitly:

```bash
npm i framer-motion
```

Then rerun `npm run test:watch`.

\"processing\" : \"done\"}&lt;/p&gt;\r\n      &lt;p data-testid=\"queued\"&gt;{queuedIncomingCount}&lt;/p&gt;\r\n      &lt;button onClick={allowPendingTransactions}&gt;Allow&lt;/button&gt;\r\n    &lt;/div&gt;\r\n  );\r\n}\r\n\r\ndescribe(\"transactions context processing states\", () =&gt; {\r\n  it(\"queues live transactions and only applies them when allowed\", async () =&gt; {\r\n    vi.useFakeTimers();\r\n\r\n    render(\r\n      &lt;TransactionsProvider&gt;\r\n        &lt;Probe /&gt;\r\n      &lt;/TransactionsProvider&gt;,\r\n    );\r\n\r\n    expect(Number(screen.getByTestId(\"total\").textContent)).toBe(TRANSACTION_COUNT);\r\n    expect(Number(screen.getByTestId(\"pending\").textContent)).toBe(TRANSACTION_COUNT);\r\n    expect(Number(screen.getByTestId(\"queued\").textContent)).toBe(0);\r\n\r\n    act(() =&gt; {\r\n      vi.advanceTimersByTime(2000);\r\n    });\r\n\r\n    expect(Number(screen.getByTestId(\"queued\").textContent)).toBe(1);\r\n    expect(Number(screen.getByTestId(\"total\").textContent)).toBe(TRANSACTION_COUNT);\r\n\r\n    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole(\"button\", { name: \"Allow\" }));\r\n    await act(async () =&gt; {\r\n      vi.advanceTimersByTime(300);\r\n    });\r\n\r\n    expect(Number(screen.getByTestId(\"queued\").textContent)).toBe(0);\r\n    expect(Number(screen.getByTestId(\"total\").textContent)).toBe(TRANSACTION_COUNT + 1);\r\n    expect(Number(screen.getByTestId(\"pending\").textContent)).toBe(TRANSACTION_COUNT + 1);\r\n    expect(screen.getByTestId(\"processing\")).toHaveTextContent(\"processing\");\r\n\r\n    vi.useRealTimers();\r\n  });\r\n});\r\n",

}

Implemented exactly that behavior.

### What changed

- Added mock transaction API with hardcoded chaos toggle:
  - New file: `portala/lib/mock-transactions-api.ts`
  - `CHAOS = false` by default
  - Only when `CHAOS` is `true`, API calls have a 10% chance to throw
  - Applied to:
    - `clearFundsApi(...)`
    - `allowQueuedTransactionsApi(...)`

- Moved transaction actions to async API-backed flows in context:
  - Updated `portala/context/transactions-context.tsx`
  - `clearFunds(transactionId)` is now async and calls mock API first
  - `allowPendingTransactions()` is async and calls mock API first
  - State updates happen only after API success

- Added TanStack Query at app level:
  - New file: `portala/app/providers.tsx`
  - Wraps app with `QueryClientProvider` + `TransactionsProvider`
  - Updated `portala/app/layout.tsx` to use `AppProviders`

- Used TanStack Query mutations for independent per-row states:
  - Updated `portala/app/page.tsx`
  - Each pending row now uses its own `useMutation` via `PendingClearAction`
    - independent loading/error state per transaction
  - Queued-approval action also uses a mutation with its own loading/error state

- Updated tests to include Query provider where needed:
  - Updated `portala/tests/transactions.page.test.tsx` with `QueryClientProvider` wrapper
  - Adjusted timer behavior to account for async mock API latency
  - Updated `portala/tests/transactions.context.test.tsx` for async allow action timing

- Added dependency:
  - `portala/package.json` now includes `@tanstack/react-query`

---

Implemented resilient concurrent clearing with TanStack + chaos-aware mock API behavior.

### What I changed

- Updated `transactions` context to use async API-backed actions:
  - `clearFunds(transactionId)` is now `Promise<void>` and calls `clearFundsApi(...)` first.
  - `allowPendingTransactions()` is now `Promise<void>` and calls `allowQueuedTransactionsApi(...)`.
  - State only updates after successful API response.

- Added independent per-transaction TanStack mutation handling in the UI:
  - New `RowClearAction` component in `portala/app/page.tsx`.
  - Each row gets its own `useMutation` keyed by transaction id (`["clear-funds", id]`).
  - Failures are logged with `console.error(...)` and shown inline as `Failed`.

- Added resilient concurrent batch clear using TanStack:
  - `clearBatchMutation` runs `Promise.allSettled(...)` over all selected/pending ids.
  - Every transaction attempts to clear concurrently (no fail-fast).
  - Failed transaction IDs are logged individually with error details.
  - Successful ones resolve independently and update immediately.

- Kept existing queue-allow flow under TanStack mutation:
  - `allowQueuedMutation` now handles queued approvals and logs errors.

### Important note

You still have one IDE error until deps are installed locally:

- `Cannot find module '@tanstack/react-query'...`

Run from `portala`:

- `npm install`
- `npm run test` or `npm run test:watch`

If you want, I can also add a small “Batch result” toast/banner (e.g., `12 cleared, 2 failed`) after each batch run.

_**User (2026-02-27 22:44Z)**_

Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client. As a result this tree will be regenerated on the client. This can happen if a SSR-ed Client Component used:
- A server/client branch `if (typeof window !== 'undefined')`.
- Variable input such as `Date.now()` or `Math.random()` which changes each time it's called.
- Date formatting in a user's locale which doesn't match the server.
- External changing data without sending a snapshot of it along with the HTML.
- Invalid HTML tag nesting.

It can also happen if the client has a browser extension installed which messes with the HTML before React loaded.

See more info here: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/react-hydration-error

---

Fixed the hydration mismatch by adding a client hydration guard in `portala/app/page.tsx`.

### What changed
- Added `isHydrated` state:
  - `false` on server + first client render
  - set to `true` in `useEffect` after mount
- While not hydrated, page renders a stable loading shell:
  - avoids server/client HTML differences from:
    - random transaction generation
    - `Date.now()` relative time labels
    - locale-based formatting differences

This removes the “server rendered text didn’t match client” issue for this page.

### One remaining IDE error
You still need dependencies installed for types to resolve:
- `Cannot find module '@tanstack/react-query'...`

Run in `portala`:
- `npm install`

---

Added the failed-clear popup flow in `portala/app/page.tsx`.

### What it does now
- Tracks failed clear attempts per transaction in page state.
- On any failed **single clear**:
  - logs error (existing behavior)
  - records attempt (timestamp + message)
  - auto-opens popup for that transaction.
- On failed **batch clear** (concurrent with `Promise.allSettled`):
  - logs each failed transaction
  - records attempt for each failed id
  - opens popup for a failed transaction.
- In pending-row actions, if a transaction has failures, it shows an `Attempts: N` button.
  - Clicking it opens the popup again for that transaction.

### Popup content
- Transaction short id
- Number of failed attempts
- Chronological attempt list with time + error message
- Close button

Only remaining IDE/lint warning is still the dependency resolution one for `@tanstack/react-query` until you run `npm install`.
